## Step 4: backlog report

Step 4 changes no files. The stats script already ran, and the triage steps are read-only. I would not wait for an answer. I put the proposal in the completion batch and go on to step 5.

`aged >45d:` is 2, so I run the triage rubric's steps 1–4 against `specs/deferred_items.md`:

- I group the 26 open items by theme and sort each by its recorded `Size:`.
- I have no tools this turn, so I have not run a concrete check on any item. I propose no **Retire** and no `→ triggered` note, because I have no evidence for either.
- I propose no **Hold**. None of the items shown carries a `Revisit if:` line or a `→ held` note.
- I execute no disposition. Only `/deferred` does that.

### Step 5 (read-only part, next)

<command>
uv run ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/scripts/deferral_scan.py scan specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md specs/dock-alerts.md
</command>

I resolve each line it lists with an `→ item:` marker, or I ask you for `→ dropped:`. Then I run `git mv` on the plan, write the history entry, and make the `chore(specs): retire plan 12` commit. The spec retires too only if no other live plan in `specs/plans/` implements `dock-alerts`.

## Message to my partner

**Plan 12 (dock-alerts): all 4 tasks are done and the final review is resolved. Deferred items are filed.**

**Backlog:** `Deferred backlog: 26 open, 51 ever closed (closure rate 66%), aged >45d: 2.` The backlog is above the 20-item volume threshold. The age spread is 0–14d: 12, 15–30d: 12, 46–90d: 2. The oldest open item is 61 days old.

**Deferred by this plan** (section `12-dock-alerts`):
- Alert emails repeat when a dock flaps between 2 and 3 free slots (final review, unfixed). Size: plan.
- Alert threshold is a constant in `alerts/notify.py`, not config (Task 3 step 6, skipped). Size: quick-fix.

**Triage proposal.** Read-only; nothing has been changed.

*Aged items, both unused carry (these gate the merge, see below):*
- 3-station-geocoding, 2026-09-09, 61d: Geocoder cache never expires for moved stations. Quick fix.
- 4-api-limits, 2026-09-20: Public status API has no per-key rate limit. Plan; rank first among plans because it is aged.

*Quick fix (13 items):*
- Dock status: poll interval is a magic number in two files; no index on `dock_id`. Together with this plan's threshold-to-config item, these three are one config and DB tidy.
- Truck routes: the export drops stops with no free docks; the CSV has no header row; there is no empty-load test.
- Reports: out-of-service docks are counted twice; the job does not retry on a status API timeout.
- Other: the station pin contrast check fails; notice emails have no unsubscribe link; battery readings above 100% are stored as sent.
- The geocoder cache item, listed above.

*Plan (9 items):*
- Alerts and status: the alert flapping item, in this plan's section; the closed-station-shown-as-open item on the map.
- Map: tile refetch on every refresh; untranslated pin tooltips.
- Reports: the PDF layout above 200 stations; totals not checked against the status feed.
- Notices: hard-coded two-language text; batching untested above 500 riders.
- Telemetry: batches are not deduplicated on retry.
- The API rate-limit item, listed above. It ranks first.

*Design (4 items):*
- Rebalance targets ignore weekday demand.
- Quiet hours ignore the rider's time zone.
- A stuck-sensor dock reports free slots forever.
- No alert for a bike battery that stays low for 3 days. This one and the stuck-sensor item are both about detecting bad dock or bike data, so they could share a design.

*Hold, Retire, Triggered:* none proposed. I can't verify any signal or item premise this turn.

**What you need to decide.** The aged-tail gate applies when I finish the branch, because `aged >45d` is 2. Before any merge or PR I'll ask you, for each of the two aged items, either to run `/deferred` on it or to carry it with a reason. I won't write an acknowledgement without a reason from you.

You can run `/deferred` on the proposal above whenever you like.

**Next:** I run the deferral scan, retire the plan, and make the retire commit. Then I run finishing-a-development-branch. There is no roadmap stage here, so there is no handoff to later stages.
